name: Paris
intro: Grand boulevards, world-class museums and riverside walks. Most sights sit along the Seine and are easy to link on foot, with the metro for longer hops.

transit.card: Navigo Easy card with metro tickets
transit.note: Metro runs from about 5:30 to after midnight, later on Friday and Saturday nights.

sources: Written from general knowledge for the MVP; needs a human review before launch

areas.name: Eiffel Tower & Trocadéro
areas.blurb: The tower, its lawns and the classic view from across the river.

areas.name: Champs-Élysées & Arc de Triomphe
areas.blurb: The grand avenue between the Arc and Place de la Concorde.

areas.name: Louvre & Tuileries
areas.blurb: The palace museum and its formal garden.

areas.name: Opéra & Grands Boulevards
areas.blurb: The opera house and the big department stores.

areas.name: Saint-Germain & Invalides
areas.blurb: Impressionists, Napoleon's tomb and Left Bank cafés.

areas.name: Notre-Dame & Île de la Cité
areas.blurb: The two islands where Paris began.

areas.name: Latin Quarter & Luxembourg
areas.blurb: Student streets, the Panthéon and the best park for kids.

areas.name: Le Marais
areas.blurb: Old mansions, small museums and falafel.

areas.name: Montmartre
areas.blurb: The hilltop village with the white basilica.

areas.name: La Villette
areas.blurb: Science museum and big modern park in the north-east.

pois.name: Eiffel Tower
pois.costNote: Lift or stairs tickets; summit costs more
pois.why: The 330 m iron tower from 1889. Go up for the view over the whole city, or just walk under it.
pois.kid: Count the 72 scientists' names engraved under the first floor.
pois.tip: Book a timed lift slot on the official site; the stairs to the 2nd floor have shorter queues.

pois.name: Trocadéro viewpoint
pois.why: The terrace across the river with the classic full view of the tower.
pois.kid: Make the tower 'sit' on your hand for a photo.
pois.tip: Busy with photographers from mid-morning; early is calmest.

pois.name: Champ de Mars
pois.why: The long lawn under the tower: picnic spot with a playground at the far end.
pois.kid: Lie on the grass and look straight up at the tower.

pois.name: Seine river cruise (Pont de l'Alma)
pois.why: A one-hour boat loop past the Louvre, Notre-Dame and the Eiffel Tower.
pois.kid: Sit on the open top deck and wave at people on the bridges.
pois.tip: Several companies leave from here and near the tower; no booking needed outside summer.

pois.name: Arc de Triomphe
pois.why: Napoleon's victory arch at the top of the Champs-Élysées, with a roof terrace over 12 avenues.
pois.kid: Count the avenues spreading out like a star from the roof.
pois.tip: Use the underground passage to cross; never try the roundabout. 284 steps to the top.

pois.name: Champs-Élysées
pois.why: The famous avenue from the Arc down to Place de la Concorde.
pois.kid: Look back at the Arc as you walk downhill.
pois.tip: Shops are pricey; walk it rather than eat here.

pois.name: Place de la Concorde
pois.why: The city's largest square, with a 3,000-year-old Egyptian obelisk.
pois.kid: Find the golden pictures on the obelisk explaining how it was shipped.

pois.name: Louvre Museum
pois.why: The world's most visited museum: the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo and the winged Victory.
pois.kid: Do a treasure hunt: Mona Lisa, the Winged Victory and the Egyptian mummies.
pois.tip: Book a timed slot and enter through the Carrousel entrance, usually quicker than the pyramid.

pois.name: Tuileries Garden
pois.why: The formal garden between the Louvre and Concorde, with ponds and green chairs.
pois.kid: Push a wooden sailboat across the round pond (in season) and try the trampolines.

pois.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
pois.why: Monet's giant Water Lilies wrap around two oval rooms.
pois.kid: Stand in the middle and spin slowly: it's like being inside the pond.

pois.name: Palais-Royal garden & columns
pois.why: A quiet arcaded garden with the striped Buren columns in the courtyard.
pois.kid: Hop from column to column like stepping stones.

pois.name: Palais Garnier opera house
pois.why: A gilded 1875 opera house with a grand staircase and a Chagall ceiling.
pois.kid: Look for the box where the 'Phantom of the Opera' was said to sit.
pois.tip: Self-guided visits run most days unless there's a rehearsal.

pois.name: Galeries Lafayette rooftop
pois.why: Free rooftop terrace on the department store, after a look at the stained-glass dome.
pois.kid: Spot the Eiffel Tower and the opera's golden statues from the roof.

pois.name: Musée d'Orsay
pois.why: Impressionists in a former railway station: Monet, Renoir, Van Gogh.
pois.kid: Find the giant station clock and look through it at the city.
pois.tip: Go up to the 5th floor first for the Impressionists.

pois.name: Les Invalides & Army Museum
pois.why: Napoleon's tomb under a golden dome, plus suits of armour and old cannons.
pois.kid: Look down at Napoleon's huge red tomb from the balcony.

pois.name: Musée Rodin garden
pois.why: Rodin's Thinker and Gates of Hell in a rose garden.
pois.kid: Copy the Thinker's pose for a photo.
pois.tip: A garden-only ticket is cheaper.

pois.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
pois.why: The Gothic cathedral, reopened after the 2019 fire with bright, cleaned stone inside.
pois.kid: Find the gargoyles and the round rose windows.
pois.tip: Entry is free; queues move fast early in the morning.

pois.name: Sainte-Chapelle
pois.why: A 13th-century chapel whose walls are almost all stained glass.
pois.kid: Each window tells a story in pictures: find Noah's Ark.
pois.tip: Best on a sunny day; book a time slot to skip the security queue.

pois.name: Shakespeare and Company
pois.why: A famous English bookshop facing Notre-Dame.
pois.kid: Find the reading nook upstairs with the old piano.

pois.name: Luxembourg Gardens
pois.why: The Left Bank's grand garden: palace, pond, puppet theatre and a big playground.
pois.kid: Rent a toy sailboat on the pond in front of the palace (in season).
pois.tip: The playground has a small fee but is worth it.

pois.name: Panthéon
pois.why: A domed temple where France buries its heroes, with Foucault's pendulum swinging inside.
pois.kid: Watch the pendulum show the Earth turning.

pois.name: Jardin des Plantes & Evolution Gallery
pois.why: Botanical garden with the Grand Gallery of Evolution: a parade of stuffed animals under a glass roof.
pois.kid: Find the elephant leading the animal parade.

pois.name: Catacombs of Paris
pois.why: Tunnels lined with the bones of six million Parisians.
pois.kid: Spooky: best for older kids who like history.
pois.tip: Timed tickets only, often sold out; 243 steps in total.

pois.name: Place des Vosges
pois.why: Paris's oldest planned square: red-brick houses around a lawn.
pois.kid: Count the 36 houses around the square.

pois.name: Musée Carnavalet
pois.why: Free museum of Paris history in two old mansions.
pois.kid: Find the old shop signs hanging in the first rooms.

pois.name: Stravinsky Fountain
pois.why: A pool of colourful moving sculptures next to the Centre Pompidou building.
pois.kid: Which sculpture is the elephant? Which one is the treble clef?

pois.name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
pois.why: The white basilica on the city's highest hill, with a free view over Paris.
pois.kid: Ride the little funicular up instead of the 200+ steps.
pois.tip: Watch for bracelet sellers on the steps: keep walking.

pois.name: Place du Tertre
pois.why: The artists' square at the top of Montmartre.
pois.kid: Watch a portrait being painted.

pois.name: Moulin Rouge
pois.why: The cabaret's famous red windmill, at the foot of Montmartre.
pois.tip: Outside only; shows are for adults.

pois.name: Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie
pois.why: Huge hands-on science museum with a planetarium and a children's city.
pois.kid: The Cité des Enfants zones are made for ages 2–12.
pois.tip: Book the Cité des Enfants slot when buying your ticket.

pois.name: Parc de la Villette
pois.why: Big modern park with themed gardens and a dragon slide.
pois.kid: Find the red folly buildings and the dragon slide.

pois.name: Rue Cler market street
pois.why: A pedestrian street of bakeries, cheese and fruit shops near the tower.
pois.kid: Pick a picnic for the Champ de Mars.

pois.name: Angelina tea room
pois.why: Belle Époque tea room famous for thick hot chocolate and the Mont-Blanc pastry.
pois.tip: Queues at weekends; the shop counter is faster for takeaway.

pois.name: Rue des Rosiers falafel
pois.why: The Marais street for stuffed falafel pittas: quick and cheap.
pois.tip: Most falafel shops close on Saturdays.

pois.name: Rue Mouffetard market street
pois.why: A sloping old street of market stalls, crêperies and bakeries.
pois.kid: Get a crêpe to eat while walking downhill.

pois.name: Saint-Germain cafés
pois.why: The Left Bank's historic cafés, such as Café de Flore and Les Deux Magots.
pois.tip: Pricey: a coffee and croque-monsieur is the classic.

pois.name: Montmartre cafés
pois.why: Small bistros around the hilltop lanes; quieter one street back from Place du Tertre.

pois.name: Bouillon Chartier
pois.why: A 19th-century dining hall serving cheap French classics.
pois.tip: No bookings at lunch; the queue moves fast.

dayTrips.name: Palace of Versailles
dayTrips.from: RER C to Versailles Château Rive Gauche (from central stations such as Saint-Michel or Musée d'Orsay)
dayTrips.why: The Sun King's palace: Hall of Mirrors, royal apartments and huge gardens with fountains.
dayTrips.tip: Book a timed palace ticket. Closed on Mondays. The gardens are free on most non-fountain-show days.

dayTrips.name: Disneyland Paris
dayTrips.why: Two theme parks east of the city, the station is at the gate.
dayTrips.tip: Buy dated tickets online; they are cheaper than at the gate.

dayTrips.name: Giverny (Monet's garden)
dayTrips.from: Train from Gare Saint-Lazare to Vernon-Giverny, then shuttle bus
dayTrips.why: Monet's house and the water-lily garden with the green Japanese bridge.
dayTrips.tip: Open from spring to autumn only; book a garden time slot.

dayTrips.name: Château de Fontainebleau
dayTrips.from: Train from Gare de Lyon to Fontainebleau-Avon, then local bus
dayTrips.why: A royal castle used by kings for 800 years, with a forest of rocks to climb.
dayTrips.tip: The château is closed on Tuesdays.

tips.title: Getting around
tips.text: Buy a Navigo Easy card at any metro station and load metro tickets onto it. Children aged 4–9 pay a reduced fare, under-4s ride free. Google Maps and the RATP app show live times.

tips.title: Museums
tips.text: Under-18s get into the national museums (Louvre, Orsay, Orangerie and more) free, but still need a timed ticket. Many museums close on Monday or Tuesday.

tips.title: Meal times
tips.text: Lunch is about 12:00–14:00 and many restaurants close until dinner at 19:30. Bakeries are the fast lunch. Ask for 'une carafe d'eau' for free tap water.

tips.title: Safety
tips.text: Pickpockets work the metro, the Eiffel Tower and Sacré-Cœur. Ignore petition clipboards and bracelet sellers. Emergency number: 112.

tips.title: Book ahead
tips.text: Eiffel Tower lifts, the Louvre, Sainte-Chapelle and the Catacombs sell timed tickets: buy on the official sites.
